styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Fort McHenry, the Star-Spangled Banner and the old harbor.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Walters, the BMA and the American Visionary Art Museum.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Crab cakes, Chesapeake seafood and Fells Point taverns.

stays.why: Walk to the National Aquarium, the historic ships and Fort McHenry ferries. Easiest base for first-timers.
Cobbled waterfront streets full of pubs and seafood. Quiet at night, close to the harbor.
Museums, the Washington Monument and grand old streets. Good value and central.
Local restaurants and a hilltop view over the harbor. Short walk to the Inner Harbor.

food: Order a Maryland crab cake: mostly lump crab, little filler. Prices vary by season, so check the menu.
Try steamed blue crabs in summer. They are messy and sold by the pound; ask for a table outside.
Fells Point has old waterfront taverns and seafood spots. Book ahead on weekend evenings.
Cheap eats: pit beef sandwiches and crab soup at local delis and markets, often under $15.
Lexington Market is a good lunch stop for local stalls. Check opening days before you go.
more_time: Add a day for Fort McHenry and the Star-Spangled Banner story; check the ferry or bus times on the day.
Train to Washington, D.C. from Penn Station takes about an hour on MARC or Amtrak. Easy day trip.
Art lovers can swap a harbor afternoon for the Baltimore Museum of Art and the Walters Art Museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the harbor, Fort McHenry and a museum or two, with time for a proper crab dinner.

month_notes: Cold and often grey; highs near 6°C. Pack a warm coat for harbor walks.
Still cold, highs around 8°C. Indoor museums are the safe bet.
Milder, highs near 12°C. Rain on about 11 days, so bring a jacket.
Spring warms up to 18°C. Good walking weather with some rain.
Pleasant at 23°C. One of the rainiest months, so keep an indoor plan.
Warm and humid, highs near 28°C. Crab season is on.
Hot and sticky, highs around 30°C. Plan outdoor sights for morning.
Similar to July: hot, humid and often wet. Carry water.
Warm and comfortable at 26°C. A good month for the waterfront.
Crisp and dry-ish at 20°C. Fewer rain days; great for walking.
Cooler at 13°C. Layers help; rain on about 8 days.
Cold again, highs near 9°C. Holiday lights and indoor sights.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold winters, warm humid summers, and mild spring and fall. Rain falls year-round.

items.title: Best time: April, May, September and October
items.text: Highs of 18–26°C and comfortable evenings. Ideal for the harbor and Fort McHenry.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid
items.text: July and August reach about 30°C with muggy air. Do outdoor sights early and stay in the shade.

items.title: Winter is cold
items.text: January highs near 6°C and lows below freezing. Bring a warm coat and gloves.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Expect rain on 8–15 days each month. Summer is wettest; a small umbrella helps.

items.title: Long summer days
items.text: June to August gives the most daylight for walking the waterfront in the evening.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobbled streets. Add sunscreen and a hat for summer.

transit.best: Walk the harbor and Fells Point; use the free Circulator bus and light rail for the rest.

modes.text: The subway and light rail cost $2 per ride; a day pass is $4.60. The light rail runs from BWI Airport to the Inner Harbor in about 30 minutes for $2.
MTA buses cost $2 per ride, $4.60 for a day pass. The Charm City Circulator is free and links the harbor, Fells Point and Mount Vernon.
Uber and Lyft both operate widely. Taxis are metered but less common.
Driving is optional. Parking downtown runs about $5 per hour near the harbor.
The Inner Harbor, Fells Point and Federal Hill are close together and easy on foot in mild weather.
MARC and Amtrak trains connect Penn Station to Washington, D.C. in about an hour.
